messages:
incident-bot: PAGER: Sev2 — GPU capacity exhaustion in prod-usw2. Autoscaler failing to add GPU nodes; request queue growing, 503s on /v1/generate increasing. Pager: @alex (on-call). Please acknowledge. :pager:

alex (on-call): Ack — I'm looking. Observability: queue length ~1.2k, p50 latency up 3x, errors hitting customers. Linking grafana: https://grafana.redwood/prod-usw2/gpu-pool

maria (sre): I see cluster-autoscaler errors in logs: attempts to create node group failed with IAM errors. Also seeing taint mismatch on new launch template (gpu:NoSchedule) so pods never land when nodes get created.

samir (eng-runtime): Pasting cluster-autoscaler error snippet:```
E0421 14:12:33.123456 1 scaleup.go:574] unable to create nodegroup: CreateAutoScalingGroup failed: UnauthorizedOperation: iam:PassRole
	status code: 403, request id: 1234-abcdef
```

alex (on-call): So two separate things: 1) IAM/PassRole preventing ASG/launch template creation, 2) taint/launch-template mismatch so even if nodes come up, pods won't schedule. Which one is blocking autoscale at the moment?

maria (sre): The IAM error is blocking new nodegroup creation entirely — autoscaler is retrying and marks scale-up as failed. There are a few pre-created GPU nodes but they're saturated.

ops-bot: Action required: runbook https://wiki.redwood/runbooks/gpu-autoscale -> step 2 (verify launch template role).

samir (eng-runtime): Quick repro of the error from our side: kube-controller tried to call AWS to create ASG but role in launch template is arn:aws:iam::999999:role/old-gpu-role which was rotated last week. New deploy updated IAM names but autoscaler config still points to old role.

alex (on-call): Can we patch autoscaler to point to the working launch template/version? If yes, do it — we need capacity now.

maria (sre): I can manually create a fallback nodegroup via the console using the correct launch template and instance profile (role: role/gpu-node-profile-v2). That should bypass the PassRole failure while infra fixes autoscaler config. Creating now, will pin min=2, desired=4.

samir (eng-runtime): While you create it, I'll adjust the cluster-autoscaler configmap to accept the new nodegroup name pattern so future scale-ups can use it. Also adding tolerance config for the gpu taint so GPU workload pods tolerate the taint on new nodes.

mike (eng-ml): Heads up — if we add nodes with a different GPU type (g4dn vs p4), model selection might fallback. I'm throttling heavy model routes at edge to prefer smaller models to reduce token load. Putting a temporary route override:```
/serve-model -> prefer model: redwood-small-gpu when pool=degraded
```

anne (cs): Customer impact: CS dashboards show 12 active customers experiencing degraded inference (timeouts, 5xx). I'm drafting an incident message to customers and will wait 10m for mitigation updates before sending.

maria (sre): Fallback nodegroup creation: console completed, nodes registering now. kubelet shows nodes with label node.kubernetes.io/instance-type=g4dn.xlarge and taint redwood/gpu=true:NoSchedule. Scheduling still blocked for pods that don't have tolerations.

samir (eng-runtime): I applied a toleration to the GPU workload daemonset / deployment so existing pods can schedule onto these tainted nodes:```yaml
spec:
  template:
    spec:
      tolerations:
      - key: "redwood/gpu"
        operator: "Equal"
        value: "true"
        effect: "NoSchedule"
```
This will let pending pods land. Rolling restart applied.

alex (on-call): After toleration + fallback nodes, are pending pods scheduling? Any error remain?

maria (sre): Pending queue dropped from 1.2k to ~240 in 8 minutes. 5xx rate decreased 60%. Some pods still crashlooping with OOM on g4dn.xlarge — need smaller batch sizes.

mike (eng-ml): Lowering batch size on affected model endpoints by 30% and enabling CPU fallback for small requests. Also enabling model-quality guardrail offload to reduce memory use. Doing that now.

anne (cs): Notified a subset of impacted customers with a short message: "We're experiencing GPU capacity issues causing higher latency. We're working on mitigation; some requests may be served on reduced capacity models. No data exposure. Will update in 30m."

ops-bot: Audit note: created fallback nodegroup "gpu-fallback-v2" id: ng-0a1b2c3d.

samir (eng-runtime): Cluster-autoscaler configmap patched to include new nodegroup regex and updated launchTemplate name. Also pushed a hotfix to controller to avoid using deprecated role name; PR 3421 created.

maria (sre): We still have the root cause: original launch template references rotated IAM role. I'm opening an infra ticket to update the original LT and restore autoscaler permissions. Ticket: INFRA-7293.

alex (on-call): Handing off to maria for the next 60m to complete cleanup and verify autoscaler resumes normal behavior. I'll be available if needed. @maria please own the postmortem. :hand: 

maria (sre): Ack — I'll run through runbook, validate autoscaler health, and confirm nodes scale down safely. If autoscaler resumes, we'll decommission gpu-fallback nodegroup.

mike (eng-ml): Early metrics: request success rate up from 78% -> 92% after nodes + tolerations + batch tuning. Good improvement but watch for regressions.

anne (cs): Customer follow-up plan: status update in 30m, then a 4hr summary. I flagged the enterprise accounts with active incidents.

samir (eng-runtime): Note for postmortem: make sure autoscaler config references are templated and validated during IAM rotations. Add an automated test that simulates role rename.

maria (sre): Current status: mitigation in place, capacity restored to 80% of expected. Autoscaler remains in degraded state until infra fixes launch template IAM. Next steps: INFRA-7293 owner to patch LT, update ASG role, run a scale test. Postmortem scheduled in #postmortems tomorrow 10:00 PT.

alex (on-call): Thanks all. Leaving the channel for handoff. If anything changes escalate to Sev1.

incident-bot: Incident updated to "mitigated" (partial): capacity restored via gpu-fallback nodegroup; autoscaler degraded. Postmortem ticket created: PM-1783000000.

ops-bot: Reminder: please add runbook checklist entries and timelines to the postmortem doc. :memo:
